predictions.text: Boston have allowed 22 goals in eleven games, the tightest defensive record on this board, and at TD Garden they have conceded six in five while scoring 21. Their overall mark is 8-2-1 and their last ten read 7-2-1. San Jose's record was not on the standings page, so the Sharks are assumed average and nothing more. Even then Boston's price of -291 breaks the brief's -250 floor, which is why the graded selection is the puck line rather than the outright: Boston -1.5 at +105.

Carolina arrive on 18 points from twelve games, with 47 goals scored and only 33 conceded. The road record is the part that matters here: six wins from eight away games and a 34-23 goal split. St. Louis were not on the standings page this session, so the Blues are treated as league average rather than credited or penalised. Even on that cautious view the Hurricanes are the clear side: Carolina to win the money line at -250.

Edmonton are the hottest side on the board: 8-1-1 for 17 points, 47 goals for and 32 against, five wins from five on the road and a three-game winning streak. At Rogers Place they are 3-1-1. Toronto's numbers were unavailable, so the Leafs are assumed average. Even so the fair money line lands at -358, far beyond the floor the brief sets, and the puck line is the only band-eligible way in: Edmonton -1.5 at +105.

Vegas are 8-4-0 with 46 goals for and 36 against, and they have won seven of ten. The concern is direction: they arrive on a two-game losing streak and are 3-2-0 on the road. Columbus were not readable, so the Blue Jackets are priced as a league-average home side. That still leaves Vegas the better team on the numbers, and the fair price of -185 sits comfortably inside the band: Vegas to win at -185.

The Rangers are the strangest profile on the board: 6-0-0 at home with 29 goals for and 10 against, but 1-4-1 on the road with eight goals scored and 19 conceded in six games. This is a road game. Ottawa were not readable, so Ottawa are assumed average. That is still enough to tilt the price, because a Rangers team scoring eight goals in six road games gives the home side the edge on the split alone. Ottawa to win at -159.

Seattle are 7-3-1 for 15 points, 6-3-1 across ten and winners of two straight, with a 4-2-1 road record. Minnesota are 6-3-2 for 14 points but only 2-3-2 away from home, though they are 4-0-0 at home, so the venue switch matters. With both records read from the league feed, Seattle come out a 56% home side and the fair price is -128: Seattle to win is the selection.

Medvedev reached this final with a 6-3 first set before Alexander Bublik retired, so the top seed has played barely a set of tennis while Basilashvili needed three sets to beat seventh seed Stefanos Tsitsipas 6-4 6-7(5) 6-3. Freshness plus the seeding points one way, and the price of -245 is inside the brief's band while still reflecting a real chance of an upset. Selection: Medvedev to win the final at -245.

Fritz, the second seed, beat fourth seed Tommy Paul 6-3 7-5 and has dropped one set in the semi-final stage; Musetti, seeded sixth, needed three sets to see off top seed Flavio Cobolli 4-6 6-2 7-5. The seedings and the shorter semi-final favour Fritz, but only mildly, because Musetti has just beaten the top seed. Our fair price is -122, which is why this one is graded medium: Fritz to win at -122.

Game 2 of the World Series at American Family Field, first pitch 00:00Z, with Logan Henderson starting for Milwaukee against Drew Rasmussen for Tampa Bay. Milwaukee lead the series 1-0 and hold home field. Only one game of postseason form was readable, so the price is deliberately conservative: the Brewers are a 55% home side and the selection is Milwaukee on the money line at -120.

Toronto Kings hold nine of the ten win tips OLBG displays on this T20, which is about as one-sided as a crowd gets, and the fair price of -195 simply reflects that weight of support. No board page for the competition could be read this session, so the number should be judged as market structure rather than form. Selection: Toronto Kings to win at -195.

North West Dragons have eight of the nine win tips on the provincial T20, and the desk's price of -170 follows that support rather than any record it could confirm. The counterweight is that a near-unanimous crowd in a low-liquidity provincial match is usually a thin signal. Selection: North West Dragons at -170, with the caveat that no provincial union page was readable.

The second women's ODI between India and Zimbabwe carries a split market: three of five tips sit on Smriti Mandhana as top India batsman, while the match itself is untipped at this read. With no series scoreline available, the desk prices India Women at 68% purely on the strength of the fixture and the gap between the two sides' standing in the format. Selection: India Women at -215.

Salthill-Knocknacarra carry 28 of 47 tips in the Galway senior final, a much softer lean than the Cork game, and they are backed at +3.50 with the handicap start. Without a county board page to confirm the throw-in, the desk treats the handicap as the safer expression of the crowd's view. Selection: Salthill-Knocknacarra +3.50 at -150.

Nemo Rangers take 27 of the 31 tips on the Cork senior football final, with the crowd backing them at +1.50 on the handicap. The GAA's national fixture page did not publish the club final and the Cork county site redirected to its schools hub, so the price rests on the handicap line and that support. Selection: Nemo Rangers +1.50 at -180.

Magdeburg host Kriens-Luzern in Champions League round seven and the desk gives them a six-and-a-half goal start against a Swiss side making the trip midweek. The fixture is confirmed by the EHF, but no group table was read, so the handicap is a neutral estimate and the confidence ceiling is medium. Selection: Magdeburg -6.5 at -120.

Fuchse Berlin face Partizan in the same round. Our line of -8.5 is the widest handicap on the handball board: it prices the gap in squad resources rather than any table position, since no group standings page was read. Berlin -8.5 at -125, capped at low confidence.

Trentino and Cisterna open the Italian round with the crowd split six tips to one in favour of Cisterna, which is a strange read for a home side with Trentino's recent record in the competition. With the league's standings page returning an error, the desk ignores that split and prices the home side at 60% on venue alone. Selection: Trentino to win at -150.

Perugia host Pordenone in the same round and the desk's 63% home estimate is the highest on the volleyball board, built from the venue and the relative depth of the two squads rather than a table. Pordenone carry six of seven tips, so this is a rare case where the price and the crowd disagree. Selection: Perugia at -170.

Denver hold eight of ten tips for the visit of New Orleans, and -180 is the shortest price on the basketball board. No record, rest situation or injury report could be checked: the league's own scoreboard feed refused every request. The number is therefore a market-structure estimate. Denver Nuggets at -180.

Atlanta have five of six tips against Houston, and the desk prices them at 62% on the basis of home venue and the crowd's lean, which is all that could be supported without a league record. Houston's road form is the obvious counter-argument and cannot be checked here. Selection: Atlanta Hawks at -165.

Ross Smith has all five win tips on the European Championship match against Luke Woodhouse, and the price of -140 is a straight conversion of that support with a margin for the crowd being one-eyed. The PDC's tournament page served a consent wall instead of the draw, so no scoring average or head-to-head could be added. Selection: Ross Smith at -140.

Harlequins take four of the five tips for the London derby against Saracens, a modest lean in a fixture that is usually close, and the desk prices the home side at 55%. With no league page read, nothing is claimed about selection, injuries or table position. Selection: Harlequins at -120.

New South Wales carry nine of twelve tips on the 2027 State of Origin series, and the price of +205 is the desk's conversion of that support. This is a ten-month outright with no team news and no venue, so it is listed for completeness rather than as a serious match pick. Selection: New South Wales to win the 2027 series at +205.
